== Original post ==

'''Europe - SYCFA Manipulation - Day 3'''
* '''Author:''' David "Lirkas 'DDM'" Destefanis
* '''Published:''' August 31, 2005
* '''Rating:''' 4.82
* '''Description:''' Counters and surprises the opponent. Going to be my deck for Day 3. Named DS deck of Day 3 Consolation Tournament.

=== Strategy ===

Overall Idea:

This deck was invented 3 days before the EC 2005� Which means it took me some time to finally get the inspiration to play something weird, yet again effective and totally new.

The first version was about 10-12 cards different, and sent to Yoda (Hungarian champ) for him to test, and I got indeed some feedback, but the basic idea is there: drain, retrieve a ton, a slap of Fear damage, drain cancelling and a shield-pulling ability which hurts... a lot.

During the EC 2005, the deck went 5-1 (me and Fabien were playing it), losing to a FULL space WYS (V), while getting only 1 ISD in hand during the first 3 turns. The deck was also less sturdy in space that it is now.

Why a deck like this ?

In a meta where you had usually Mains (V10 was just out, and there was not much WYS (V) yet), we figured out that going to space, with some manipulation and nasty tricks was the way to go. Especially with retrieval.

With the arrival of WYS (V), we tweaked the deck just slightly, since the engine is so strong that to meta vs. anything you just need to add THE counter or meta card, and that's all. Now this deck vs. WYS (V) just go for the jugular vein, which is a turn 2 beatdown on their system, which is done quite easily all the time with 2 ISD, 2 Squadrons (at least), All Power To Weapons and Lateral Damage.

Anyway, the control ability of this deck is amazing. It is a total different take on the brutal approach of usual SYCFA Fear, and surprises the opponent throughout the game, usually earning the win.

However, I would not play this after giving away the decklist, since much is about surprise, even though it is still very solid even if you know what is coming.

About this Version:

This was supposed to be my Dark deck during Day 3, had I managed to qualify. I didn't (I came 8th but I was put down to 9th place after the PC realized a mistake at the last moment on scoring), but the goal was pretty wicked: surprise the opponent with this unexpected deck, earning a possible win in a scenario where the opponent is not often expecting such cards or decks.

Even if I did get a loss, it would never be a HUGE loss, since I had all this retrieve, inserts, and Fear damage. Thus, since I knew I would win with more differential with my MBO (indeed it never lost a single game), it would still allow me to get into the WC 2005 finals, winning them in the hand.

The deck list was also tuned specifically for Day 3, not Day 3 consolation tournament. I was too lazy to change it and I thought it was better to keep it "as it is� to see how it would have fared.

The main change would have been a Dead Ewok (V) added in, since you can't allow yourself to face an Elorrs Madak (V) deck like AitC (V).

This deck went 1-2 during Day 3 consolation tournament. Pretty weird, considering I faced the 2 worst match-ups for the deck: AitC (V) and MBO. I won against MBO (but then, I knew what to do) and I lost a close one vs  AitC (V) (but look on the match-ups section). The other game lost was vs. a TRM deck, where my starting hand and the next one during turn 2 were awful, and the opponent's was good (Phylo starting hand). Still, even though I got owned and was losing some 45 to 6, I managed to come back and lost only by 19.

This deck was still praised by all my opponents there, getting a lot of compliments about the wickedness and the cleverness of it. I can't thank enough all of you for this.

Like the deck list says, I was not playing Dead Ewok (V) on Day 3, but Tarkin's Orders, since I thought to face a lot of TRM, that would drain a lot on the Death Star.

Last note: Monnok was NOT in the deck list Day 3, there was instead a Pride Of The Empire. But I understood afterwards that you CANNOT play this immediate effect with this deck, since it deploys on a starfighter, and not a squadron. However before putting Pride Of The Empire, there was a Monnok, so here it is again.

Start:

The deck, like my MBO, has no room for side starts. There is only one start possible, and this is the following:

You Cannot Hide Forever & Mobilization Points (SE)

Kuat Drive Yards (V) (SE)

Dreaded Imperial Fleet (V) (SE)

YCHF&MP is used always as a first action to get Wakeelmui (or Carida if you have Wakeelmui into hand). Then, if your opponent pulls DDTA shield (or before, if playing TRM), you're cruising, since you've just begun your shield pulling strategy.

Anyway, second action (or as soon as you drop a ship in space, usually waiting anyway the opponent's turn so to have your used pile back under your reserve) pull Crossfire (V) by losing YCHF&MP.

Now activate your 5+ force, use SYCFA to pull the War Room, and  to check what is in your force pile / Reserve deck.

Play Crossfire (V) on table.

If you have enough force and some good space power in hand, you can get and play Sienar Fleet System with Crossfire (V), deploy a system with KDY (V) (and/or from your hand), drop an ISD (from 4 to 6 cost), get a TIE Squadron from reserve, thus retrieving your 3 lost force, and get ready to start draining.

The next few turns are about pulling your other effects for drain cancelling, fear damage, and beatdown (Lateral Damage).

Note however that it is often better not to do anything until you have at least 2 ISD into hand, since without ISD in hand you have no space power.

This means that usually, it is better to set-up turn 1, without deploying anything but locations, and get some 3-4 cards to have a better hand.

During the Game:

With 3 Unexpected Interruption, 2 WMAOP, and some interrupts, you should be able to get whatever effect or interrupt you need in hand.

This is particularly important.

Unexpected Interruption is often played in AOBS, but the real deck that started using is was SYCFA Tie Interceptors, since this DS had retrieval.

Here there is TIE retrieval too, so the interrupt fit in again.

This is because this saves you card slots. You do not need anymore 5 All Powers To Weapon to battle in space (interrupts useless if the opponent does not come, also), or 300 Twi'lek to get your effects.

Unexpected Interruption gets everything for you: your 1 copy of interrupt, or your effect puller (and thus your effect).

So really, packing only 1 Fear Will Keep Them In Line (V) was like packing 6, since you had 2 WMAOP and 3 Unexpected Int. to get WMAOP.

Same with interrupts.

Pretty strong, if you're activating a lot (which this deck does).

Then there is A Dangerous Time, to prevent the opponent to draw anything useful and to make him pull a shield (yes, there is a shield that cancel this interrupt), Overwhelmed (combo with Lateral Damage) to wipe out an entire fleet, etc.

The whole goal of this interrupt is two-fold: force the opponent into playing a shield, or just plainly manipulate his force pile everyturn.

This can mean the difference between a huge win and a huge loss.

The SYCFA objective allows you to get your Death Star Trooper to cancel drains with Strategic Reserves.

Vengeance at the main system where your opponent is battling you, etc.

Soon enough, the opponent will have pulled all his shields (Battle Plan, Grabber, Aim High, DDTA, or the anti-A Dangerous Time shield) and you will be able to hit him with a full 12 force loss insert thanks to the destiny 3 troopers (become destiny 5 with Raithal).

This huge force loss worked twice during Day 3 Consolation tournament.

Remember to get someone (a trooper, or a squadron) to the Docking Bay: you take no battle damage here, and basically laugh at Battle Plan / Order.

The opponent will face a tough choice: battling you there, thus risking a TIE Squadron react, allowing you to retrieve 3 Force, but also probably hold the Docking Bay, or leave you alone, and in this case, you drain for free.

A word about activation:

Turn 1: 5+ what the opponent gives you. You take out the Death Star: War Room, Wakeelmui and a system with Kuat Drive Yards (V).

Turn 2: 10+ what the opponent gives you. You get another system out if needed.

This deck has some good activation, and indeed with all 4 systems out it is 16+, which is enough to do all that you have to do.

Card Choices:

Vengeance (x2) : it deploys for 9, but thanks to KDY (V) and Dreaded Imperial Fleet, the cost is 6, with immunity Accuser (x2) : also a great ship. Deploys officially for 2 as a react, but you can't pay less than 3, so�

Anyway, while reacting, this ISD lets you get also another TIE Squadron from Reserve (which means another 3 retrieval) with Dreaded Imperial Fleet (V). Speak about power.

Tyrant and Thunderflare: inside because of the low deploy cost: 7. Which means "4� really.

Imperial-Class Star Destroyer (V) (x3) : each of them deploys for 6, or 3 if with another unique ISD. This is strong, and allows you to mass deploy to the opponent to kill him (Lateral Damage ?, All Power To Weapons ?) or just to better spread and drain afterwards (Tyrant + 2 of these babies cost only 10, for a total power of 24+9, considering the squadrons, +possible 18 due to APTW ; basically, 10 force for 51 power + destiny. Or +2 destinies if you put OOP Crossfirve (V)).

Remember that Dreaded Imperial Fleet (V) is not a once a turn action: you can deploy more than one Squadron each turn, if you play more than one ISD.

7 TIE Assault Squadron: 7 is a must have. If you start cutting on these numbers, you might not find any in your reserve when deploying an ISD. Move quickly your Death Star into orbit of one of your systems to move them to the Death Star, and then land them to the DB for Battle Plan and more retrieval.

The Emperor's Shield and The Emperor's Sword : initially there were 3 copies of each, since the goal was to quickly react anywhere (even at the Death Star: Docking Bay 327 to hold it), while retrieving 3. It is however costly. They are still, however, very useful, and can be played with DIF (V) for 3 instead of 5 if you do not find any non-unique TIE Squadron there.

Death Star Trooper (x3) : stupid card, useless, but has 4 great advantages: it's non unique (playable on Strategic Reserves), it's destiny 3 (which can be boosted to 5 with Raithal), it is pullable with SYCFA during your deploy phase, and it can be retrieved into hand with Carida.

Most play the Death Star Gunner, but this is a much inferior choice.

Strategic Reserves: 3 Unexpected Interruption and 2 WMAOP mean that you will have that card soon. Better than A Bright Center To The Universe because besides Tawss Khaa (V) nothing can prevent you from cancelling drains, whereas some cards like Obi-Wan's Journal kill A Bright Center To The Universe. Also, read the following�

Carida: "if you occupy, during your control phase may lose 1 Force to retrieve a trooper into hand�.

First of all, unlike most other systems, you do not have to control it to use the game text. Occupying is enough. Secondly, there is no real cost: you're losing 1 Force, but you're retrieving 1 also (the trooper).

And you do not have to lose it from your hand, so it can be done even when you have only crucial cards remaining in hand by losing a card from Reserve, for example.

Where the card really shines, is that you will inevitably deploy the Death Star Trooper from Strategic Reserves to a Death Star location. For example, to the Death Star : DB to hold Battle Plan (with some Tie Squadron maybe ?), or to the Death Star War Room to block the drain there.

The opponent is bound to battle your trooper, and this is where you lose him into the lost pile. Well, just retrieve it next turn with Carida's game text, and you have another drain canceller for Strategic Reserves into hand.

Basically, each trooper does cancel TWO drain each time.

Raithal: gives +1 or +2 (if you control) destiny to your troopers. It does mean that you have a minimum insert total of 9, and a maximum of 15. Since you will be deploying troopers as soon as they hit Strategic Reserves, there are 2 options for the opponent: battle them to prevent you from not paying to drain, thus allowing you to take them back into hand for more drain cancelling, or leaving them alone, allowing to drain for free and to insert him. Game breaking.

Of course, if the opponent goes to Raithal, Raithal's game text is cancelled. In the unlikely even the opponent manages to activate enough without the insert popping up to allow him to deploy a fleet there, just kill him at the system.

Kiffex: a drain 2 system. Usually the first system where you deploy, since you get also the +2 to power thanks to Kiffex's game text with an ISD and a Squadron. Also, a quick deploy of FWKTIL (V) works, since it is parsec 2.

Kashyyyk: was before that Naboo. But Kashyyyk is a 2/1, so I guess it's better, even though it's a little farther away. Besides, it is one card more towards a Classic deck.

A Dangerous Time (x3) : Great card. Allows you to know the opponent's force pile (considering the amount of activation nowadays, it is equivalent to know the opponent's deck) BUT also to reorder it however you wish. Combined with Battle Plan / Order, deploy, etc, it means that your opponent will never draw a single useful card, and that you will know what he will draw.

If you add Monnok to this equation, you can understand the damage you can do (put doubles together, and kill them when the opponent draws them).

If the opponent pulls the Shield, you still are in good shape, since it is one shield less against you. If he doesn't, you can pull back next turn with Unexpected Interruption this wicked interrupt, to continue your manipulation.

Just to let you know, this interrupt is grabbed 80% of my games.

Tarkin's Orders: Basically a Strategic Reserves that you can pull with Unexpected Interruption, to cancel another drain of stupid Careful Planning decks, or TRM who come to the Death Star.

It cancels also a good number of cards, including especially Hyper Escape.

Like Jonny Chu said after playing online with Dagobah Clouds vs. me : wow, this is old school�.

Overwhelmed: was the main card in the 1st version of this deck. Cut to 1 copy. Send to used an entire fleet. Now, since the deck packs All Power To Weapons, we consider that it is better to battle damage the opponent with more Lateral Damage and APTW than to send the fleet to the Used. Still, an Overwhelmed is the solution to the most difficult problems, like if you face the Super Falcon in a MWYHL deck, or against a AitC (V) deck.

Overload: card added against decks that do like Weapons in space, like some WYS (V) or some HB (wink at Alden Peterson). Against both I usually lose a system from hand to retrieve and to track to wipe out with a tracked 0 a key ship. This allows me also to wipe out the fleet with Overwhelmed after the weapon is gone.

Else it is used to kill some more drain power for LS Mains with sabers on ground, when I'm not cancelling drains with Strategic Reserves.

All Power To Weapons: card which was not there in the EC 2005 version. Weird ? Not really, since the opponent will always fear this card (+6 power for each squadron in battle, which means that you can quickly get insane amounts of power), and thus play very carefully in space. Since it turned out that some LS decks were not so afraid to go there, a couple of APTW, which can be taken with Unexpected Interruption, are just an excellent choice.

To give you an example: the opponent jumps on your Vengeance with a TIE Assault Squadron on Kiffex with the R3 Falcon and Life Debt. You react with the Accuser (which gets another TIE Assault Squadron) and with The Emperor's Shield (or sword). You add All Power To Weapons.

The power of the opponent is 9 + 4 destinies. Yours is 42 + 1 destiny. Even drawing all 5s (which is not going to happen very often), the opponent just gets 29, which is the Falcon + 5 damage (not counting your destiny). And you have just to forfeit 2 Squadrons to cover the attrition.

We Must Accelerate Our Plans (x2) : this cards pulls your other effects, and it can be pulled with Unexpected Interruption. If you need to recycle it to have a 5 on top, just play it for free, and pull the other WMAOP with it. Note that you need only to replace BOTH interrupts with Twi'lek Advisor to get a Classic deck.

Atmospheric Assault (x3): utility card. Allows you to deploy from hand any TIE Assault Squadron stuck there (Dreaded Imperial Fleet (V) only allows you to deploy them from Reserve), instead of having to lose it to a drain, and THEN recycle it so that you can play it that way. Excellent to deploy directly a squadron to the Death Star: Docking Bay 327. With All Power To Weapons, it is another 9 free power to space.

Crossfire (V) : pulls Sienar Fleet Systems, but if for some reason you have Sienar Fleet Systems in hand, you can pull Fear Will Keep Them In Line (V) instead. The added bonus that you can add (once per game) a battle destiny whenever you wish is money too. In space, or on ground, it is just strong. Usually ditched for more overflow, or to surprise the opponent into forfeiting him his EPP who just slashed your lone trooper on the Death Star (retribution I call it).

3,720 To 1: 12 force loss. Game right here.

Lateral Damage (x2) : well, you have 5 cards to get them, like any other effect. Pretty much guaranteed to have this utinni effect quickly into hand for beatdown, then. 2 is key.

Weaknesses, Questions, and Overall Choices:

Why Kuat Drive Yards (V) ? Don't you think it hinders FWKTIL (V) ?

It does.

However, getting systems quickly is key (and getting the ones you're looking for too). I know a lot of ways to get quickly systems on table, but simply put, KDY (V) is the fastest and less card intensive (only 1 card), while giving your ISD deploy bonuses.

In half the games, there will space battles. And maybe there will be difficulties to control 2-4 systems.

The previous version had 2 Sneak Attack (V) (good also with Death Star Troopers, both used if Raithal on table, and lost) and 1 Sacrifice (V) to cancel Kuat Drive Yards (V). It turned out to be useless� This deck has some drain reduction (strategic reserves) built-in, and some huge retrieval. FWKTIL (V) will do 2 damage. It's better than nothing, and still strong. Keeping only one system under your firm grip will still mean drain of 2 and 2 force loss, while cancelling the opponent's most heavy drain. Add the retrieval and the opponent is clearly losing the game.

What if the opponent does play the insert shield or knows what you're aiming at ?

Then it does mean that he will either play the shield BEFORE I play the insert, which means that I can abuse A Dangerous Time then (or retrieval, or etc..) or that he will play one shield less, waiting for me to play the insert (and meanwhile I do abuse the other interrupts).

Anyway, inserts is just a side strategy here. It takes me 2 slots: Raithal (which still is a 2/1 system) and the insert effect. The troopers would be still played since the combo Carida / Strategic Reserves / SYCFA is just too strong.

So all in all, I'm often playing the deck as a very strong "non-insert� deck, until the opponent burns his shields out� At that moment, I hit him hard with 3,720 To 1.

I hit both TRM and MBO with that strategy during Day 3 consolation tournament.

What are the shields you make the opponent pull usually ?

The more I can.

I usually try not to deploy anyone to the Death Star: Docking Bay 327 to make the opponent pull Battle Plan for example.

The grabber is always played.

Aim High can also if the opponent is not play combo Insurrection (which happens quite often vs. a deck like this).

Don't Do That Again. Etc.

Some games, especially vs. Thrown Back (V), you can know pretty quickly if you will make the opponent pull everything or not. Adapt to the game then.

Someone could grab A Dangerous time with the Shield A Tragedy Has Occurred, why should he play the Shield against ADT ?

If he grabs A Dangerous Time, then he won't grab Atmospheric Assault, Unexpected Interruption, Overwhelmed, All Power to Weapons, Monnok, or my self-recycling WMAOP..

Fair enough for me.

You risk a lot from anti-react cards, which are often played in nowadays meta.

This is true.

A-W, Romas �Lock' Navender, Gold Leader In Gold 1 (V), all are cards that can create beatdown occasions against you.

However, Romas is played only in WYS (V) usually, and the rest is not played more than a couple of times. With A Dangerous Time x3, and Unexpected Interruption x3, it shouldn't be a problem to prevent the opponent into drawing these stupid ships into hand.

And Sense ?

Well, same here: you will know that the opponent is playing S/A. Just put them on top of opponent's force pile, and he will never draw them. And pull both anti S/A shields. The opponent will have so many things to S/A anyway, that it won't be against your reacts.

Also, only the non-combo Sense works against reacts.

Last but not least, against Sense and Gold Leader In Gold 1 (V), remember that it works once only. You can react not only with the TWO different unique squadrons, but also with the Accuser.

Anyway, yes, anti-react cards are a liability. But A Dangerous Time offsets this a lot.

I've played against heavy S/A decks (7 Sense, 4 Alter), and I've never had any problems, since if the opponent does not sense your interrupts/effects, you just play safe and pile up some ships (or squadrons, if with Vengeance), thus not needing reacts. If the opponent S/A your interrupts and effects, then he's slowing you down, but he's losing also 3 force each time, so your reacts will go through.

Match-ups:

WHAP: bad match-up. It is a drain race. During Europeans 2005 I did put Imperial Decree (V) only against this deck.

WHAP has some sort of retrieval (Secure Route (V)), and usually is strong on Sense / Alter.

Pull both shields, and abuse A Dangerous Time.

It is a drain race, since the opponent has much ground and no space, and you the opposite. Insert him if you can.

During Worlds, I knew I would not face any WHAP, so Decree (V) was taken out.

TRM: extra caution needed. TRM activates a lot, and can jump on you pretty strong. However, remember that you have A Dangerous Time, anti-S/A shields, and that in space, TRM has tricks, some power, but not THAT MUCH.

What you need to do against TRM is to play it safe, if you don't know what to expect. The first good point vs. TRM is that they usually draw big hands, and they will against Space, to get the cards needed. This allows them to set up also monstrous activation, but leaves them vulnerable to Monnok.

TRM will surely also pull DDTA shield as its first action. No big deal.

The best against TRM is to be able to get out the Vengeance with a couple of squadrons (or 1, if the TRM is without Sense, and you have a TIE Squadron react ready or Accuser react) at Kiffex.

Get out your effects, and start hitting TRM for drain of 2 plus 2 damage due to Fear Will Keep Them In Line (V). If opponent is playing heavy S/A, play both anti S/A shields and all your effects out. No need to protect SFS with some presence at Wakeelmui if you have already set-up: you have the other effects (Strategic Reserves and FWKTIL (V)) that are annoying too. You can get any effect back with WMAOP / Unexpected Interruption anyway.

The Vengeance is a lot like a cruising Ghhhk, and there is not much the opponent can do against it.

Since TRM does not spread very much, you can handle their occasional drains with Strategic Reserves / Retrieval, while pinging them to death, and destroying their fleet.

It is vital, however, that you get out some systems for activation. TRM will surely have Aim High out, and won't give you any icons. Better to have all your systems out, even if you're giving this way a billion force to the opponent: you have the advantage in space: it is your ground, so it is necessary not to get force choked.

Whenever the opponent has a space force which is, in your opinion, too strong to battle efficiently, just let it be, or Overwhelm it (with the help of Lateral Damage). TRM has not much space, and if all is at one location, you can spread out and win the drain race.

I usually do not pull the War Room against TRM. I use it to lose and retrieve to track with Overload, killing stupid Mains who like to enhance their drains with Lightsabers.

If the opponent pulls out Draw Their Fire to damage your stupid trooper trick to cancel their drains at your DB, just cancel first with Strategic Reserves, then deploy your trooper but DO NOT leave it there to cancel the next drain: just fight them and make them lose 1 (you retrieve 1). Since you retrieve into hand troopers lost with Carida, you can make a loop while still cancelling their drains there. I made the choice of inserting the opponent instead during my game vs. TRM. Which can be done, but then you are eating some heavy force drains there. Unless you pack 2 other troopers, of course.

In this game, occupying Carida is key, if the opponent has Phylo on your DB, since you will need to cancel the drains there, and to retrieve your troopers into hand.

All in all, a winnable game. And if you lose, it's not by much.

Tatooine CP (V) : these decks are made to counter Scum on Tatooine. They usually pack some anti-Scum cards, some mains, some ships, all pretty basic stuff, and sometime Celebration too.

Basically, the match-up is not a lot different from TRM, albeit a lot more easy. Holding Tatooine is the first step, since you will prevent any Celebration madness, and draining for 2 there, even though you won't be doing Fear damage. Little by little, adapt to your opponent's deck, looking for openings for battle overflow, and for drain damage.

Remember that if the opponent has nothing against reacts, you can spread out with ease, since any battle made by the opponent will result in some overflow for the opponent.

During a game, I had Tyrant + TIE Squadron on Tatooine, and the LS dropped his 6 cards hand: Luke (V), Red 5, Outrider, Dash, Millenium Falcon and Cpt Han Solo. I did react with Accuser + Squadron, and also with The Emperor's Shield.

I did add All Power To Weapons. My power was 36+destiny (due to the �6 of Outrider), his was 18+2 destinies. I lost an ISD for attrition, he lost Luke, Red 5, and some other 4 cards for battle damage, and ran away.

AitC (V) : this deck faced one during Day 3 consolation tournament. Without Dead Ewok (V) (that you can pull back with Unexpected Interruption after playing it), I knew I would 80% lose that game.

However, had I had it, I would have won it. I made my opponent grabbed A Dangerous Time turn 2, so Dead Ewok (V) would have been working and killing his drains every turn.

During this game, you have to set-up as quickly as possible, and get Resistance shield into effect (especially since you don't have Dead Ewok (V)). Then, get Overwhelmed into hand to wipe out the opponent's fleet from existence as soon as he tries to satisfy Battle Order. You'll be draining for 1+2+2+1 (6) + 2 Fear Damage. Total 8, which is about what the opponent will damage you too if holding 4 sites. Both have retrieval, so wiping you the opponent's fleet is key, because their retrieval is more sturdy than yours.

Of course, hold the Docking Bay with at least a trooper and a squadron, you can't risk losing it.

I lost the game vs AitC (V) because I lost from hand Overwhelmed thinking it was Overload to the first drain 2 (both interrupts were side by side in my hand), else I would have won the game (or at least be very close).

Still, usually you lose the match-up if you don't have Dead Ewok (V) (my opponent made some mistakes). But you don't lose it by much, which is all I was aiming at for Day 3.

Inserts usually do not work very much against AitC (V), but if they pull all their shields, it's always worth a try, especially if they have to pay for their drains.

The main problem vs. AitC (V) is that they will pull out Tawss Khaa (V), thus preventing them from cancelling your drains. Ouch.

Endor CP (V) : as Tatooine CP (V), mainly. Cancel their drains with Strategic Reserves and Tarkin's Orders. Kill their fleet if it shows up in space, or Overwhelm it. A Dangerous Time their force pile, making sure they draw nothing useful but with 3PO.

This match-up is usually in your favor, unless the force is not with you.

MBO: don't think to win this match-up. The obvious counter card is the Death Star Assault Squadron (pullable), but frankly, I do not like that card that much. It is too expensive, and against my MBO it is useless. Since Day 3 I knew I would not have faced MBO, I did not put any other counters. Of course, this was Day 3 CONSOLATION tournament, so imagine my surprise when game 1 I met CubsFan's MBO. Ugh.

I did what I could: I deployed a trooper and moved it to the Y4:DB, while I controlled Yavin 4 with Tyrant and a squadron turn 1. Then while my opponent was struggling to flip (mistake imho, you do not need to flip against SYCFA), I made him pull all his 3 shields, deployed all my troopers, and moved my ISD to Raithal, while putting some space force to the Death Star. Insert hit him for 11 Force Loss, and then, when he managed to blow the Death Star, I just reinforced my fleet there, Lateral Damaged a ship, All Power To Weapons, and made him lose, after his whole fleet, another 9/11 force overflow (I don't remember exactly how much, CubsFan will know though).

Of course, do NOT deploy the Death Star War Room against MBO. You don't want to lose some other 7 Force + the location.
